(1) the CDMA implementation achieves a 1.7dB SNR advantage over the TDMA implementation for a 4-channel system, and (2) this advantage increases to 3dB for an 8-channel system.

the use of software techniques to implement a CDMA system.
the use of software techniques to increase the number of channels in a multiplexed sensing system, and with the comparison of the performance of CDMA and TDMA.
the application of software radio techniques to sensing applications, and with the development of a new class of sensor networks that are software-defined.

CDMA outperforms TDMA for a large number of channels, but TDMA outperforms CDMA for small numbers of channels.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDMA can be used in the sensing domain to increase the number of simultaneous channels without sacrificing the signal quality.

CDMA can be used to improve SNR in the presence of noise and interference, and that this can be done without any special hardware.
